lineValue.title: Line value
lineValue.definition: It compares the odds we published with the bookmakers' consensus probability without margin, at the last capture before kick-off. Positive: we published above that fair price.
lineValue.none: There are no published picks with their closing reference yet.
lineValue.small_one: {count} pick with its reference: we do not show the mean yet.
lineValue.small_other: {count} picks with their reference: we do not show the mean yet.
lineValue.minutes: The reference was taken, as a median, {minutes} minutes before kick-off.

forecast.subtitle: The last probability before kick-off against the result, in the matches finished over the last {days} days.

forecast.binLine: When we said between {low} % and {high} %, it happened {observed} % of the time ({count} cases).
forecast.omitted: {count} cases in ranges with fewer than {min} are not shown.

how.title: How a pick is decided
how.intro: All of this must happen for there to be a pick. If nothing meets it, nothing is published that day.

steps.model: A model that has beaten the market in its own test.
steps.value: Odds that pay more than the probability says, with a recent price from several bookmakers.
steps.risk: A bounded risk: no odds too high and no probability too uncertain.
steps.context: The match read by PrediGol Intelligence that same day, with its news.
steps.one: At most one pick per match, and never to fill the day.

definitions.title: Definitions in force
definitions.subtitle: If one changes, we say it here and recompute the history with the new one.

zero.title: So far we have not published a single pick
zero.body: This page says it as it is: PrediGol publishes only when a match meets every condition and, for now, none has. We would rather not publish than publish for the sake of it.
zero.forecast: What we do measure is the forecast of the matches that already finished, with its calibration, below.

parlays.title: PrediGol's parlays
parlays.subtitle: The day's parlay and the multi-day one, counted like the picks. A parlay exists once it has its selections: a day without a parlay does not count.
parlays.none: We have not created a parlay of this kind yet.
parlays.small_one: With {count} settled parlay we do not show a return yet: the sample is too small.
parlays.small_other: With {count} settled parlays we do not show a return yet: the sample is too small.
parlays.inconclusive: With fewer than {count} settled parlays the sample does not allow a conclusion yet.
parlays.partial_one: {count} won with a selection voided, returned or half-settled.
parlays.partial_other: {count} won with a selection voided, returned or half-settled.
parlays.how: A parlay wins if all its selections win and loses if one loses. A voided or returned selection does not count as lost: the parlay goes on with the others.

picks.title: Pick by pick
picks.subtitle: Every pick we published, with the odds and the probability it was published with and how it ended. It stays as it was published: it is not changed afterwards.
picks.none: There are no published picks to list yet.
picks.legend: The odds are the ones available when the pick was chosen. «PrediGol said» is PrediGol's probability; «Market», the one the bookmakers gave without their margin.

pick.title: What a pick is
pick.what: A pick is a specific selection in a match, for example «over 2.5 goals» or «home win», that PrediGol publishes because, according to its analysis, the odds pay more than the probability says.
pick.notSure: It is not a sure prediction: it is a bet with value. It can lose and it will lose many times. What counts is the result of many picks, not of one.
pick.frozen: It is published before the match starts, with the odds of that moment, and it is not changed afterwards: it stays as it was published and the result is added beside it. PrediGol does not receive any betting money.
pick.filters: A forecast is not a value and a value is not a pick: only what passes every filter in «How it is decided» is published.

read.title: How to read probabilities and odds
read.intro: The numbers in this explanation are only an example of how to read them: they are not a pick.

odds.name: Odds
odds.text: The bookmaker's price. At odds of 2.00, for every 1 staked you would receive 2 if it wins (1 profit plus your stake). At 1.50 you would receive 1.50.

said.name: PrediGol said
said.text: How likely PrediGol thinks that selection is. 55% is not a promise: out of 100 such cases we expect about 55 to happen, not all of them.

market.name: Market
market.text: What the bookmakers say once their margin is removed. Odds of 2.00 are roughly equivalent to 50%.

value.name: Value
value.text: There is value when PrediGol gives a higher probability than the market: with 55% against 50%, odds of 2.00 would pay more than they risk if PrediGol's probability is the right one. That is why calibration and the sample matter: they measure whether those percentages come true.

units.name: Units
units.text: We count as if you staked 1 unit on every pick. +1.00 u is winning one unit; −1.00 u, losing it. PrediGol does not handle money.

results.name: Results
results.text: Won and Lost; Half won and Half lost, on Asian lines; Returned, when the stake comes back; Void, when there was no bet (for example, a match that was not played); Pending, until the match ends.

read.example: Illustrative example: odds 2.00, PrediGol said 55%, the market 50%.
